decisions.reason: The owning page places lem-brownian-transition-semigroup-property immediately after this definition, and that lemma explicitly proves both P_s P_t = P_{s+t} and the Gaussian kernel identity. The definition itself also says that the expectation form is proved by the later semigroup lemma. Thus the page interface does include the promised proof, while making the lemma depend on the notation introduced here avoids a circular dependency.

The rejection correctly identifies a space mismatch: Wiener measure lives on C([0,infinity),R), whereas Gamma is a subset of the coordinate product. The intended independence proof is sound after replacing every mu(Gamma) by mu(j^{-1}(Gamma)); taking A'=Omega then identifies this quantity with P(A), so the zero-one calculation is unchanged.

The maximum-law supplier deliberately normalizes Brownian motion on one measurable full event. Without carrying that convention into this statement, an arbitrary version may have exceptional discontinuous paths and the uncountable supremum need not be a measurable random variable. The repair adopts the supplier's representative and proves measurability from rational evaluations and continuity.

The class D consists of measurable subsets of S times T, so its Dynkin-system universe must be S times T rather than the unrelated probability sample space Omega. The rectangle argument and all section identities were otherwise valid; replacing the two ill-typed whole-space references restores the exact pi-lambda proof without changing the lemma.

The distribution supplier defines measurable hitting times only after replacing Brownian motion by an everywhere-continuous zero-start representative. The unqualified statement did not inherit that convention, so tau_a could be nonmeasurable on an uncompleted space. The repair fixes one representative, obtains positive-level measurability from the supplier, treats zero pathwise, and transfers negative levels through -B.

The cited first-passage distribution and density apply to the explicitly normalized continuous zero-start representative, not to an arbitrary pointwise version. Without that convention tau_a need not be a measurable extended random variable, so its expectation is not licensed. The repair carries the representative into the statement and F1 before integrating the density.

The Gaussian convolution and semigroup proof are correct, but the final choice audit omitted the Riemann-to-Lebesgue bridge in F3. That interface explicitly requires Countable Choice and is invoked in steps 1.1 and 6.1. The repair records F5 as supplying that choice as well as the choice used by distribution-function uniqueness.

The pathwise counterexample is correct, but the bare AC definition does not itself supply any Brownian theorem. The actual choice dependence is inherited from the Brownian one- and quadratic-variation corollary in F1. The repair records that exact interface and notes that fixing one point of its already nonempty full-measure event adds no family-of-choices use.

The proof correctly shows that the stopped exit segments E_n are iid and explicitly warns that the nested future processes W^n are not independent: W^{n+1} is a measurable remainder of W^n. Only the title conflated those objects. Renaming it to independent Brownian exit segments makes the carrier match the proved claim.

The random-horizon conditional argument was load-bearing and required L to be measurable with respect to the stopped-path sigma-algebra. The repair proves that Brownian paths have no flat interval, reconstructs {L<a} from countably many stopped coordinates, and then avoids any unproved random-kernel substitution by testing fixed horizons 1/n on the G_L-events {1-L>=1/n}.

reviews.reason: The definition introduces p_t and P_t, handles t=0, and the immediately following page item proves the asserted semigroup and probability-kernel properties. No mathematical or interface repair is needed.

Steps 1.2 and 2.1 now use the measurable inclusion j and the correctly typed pushforward probability mu(j^{-1}(Gamma)). The event-integral argument proves independence and P(A)=P(A)^2 without treating a product-space set as a Wiener-measurable subset of C.

The example now fixes the everywhere-continuous zero-start representative required by its maximum-law supplier and explicitly obtains a finite measurable M_t from the rational dense-set supremum. The probability and limit calculations then apply to exactly the normalized carrier.

Step 3.1 now proves that D contains S times T by the constant-one conditional identity, and step 4.1 uses that same product-space universe for the generating rectangle pi-system. The remaining lambda-system closure and simple-function extension are correctly typed and unchanged.

The corollary now works throughout with the exact continuous representative used by the one-sided hitting-time law. Positive hitting times are measurable by that supplier, tau_0 is identically zero, and for a<0 the pathwise equality tau_a(B)=tau_{-a}(-B) transfers both measurability and almost-sure finiteness.

The example now defines tau_a only after fixing the supplier's everywhere-continuous zero-start representative and records its measurability and almost-sure finiteness. F1 therefore supplies a genuine random-variable law with density g, and the lower-bound proof of the divergent first moment remains valid.

Step 8.1 now identifies every actual choice dependency: inherited AC in the Brownian and normal-law interfaces, and Countable Choice supplied by AC for both F3's compact Riemann/Lebesgue conversion and F4's law uniqueness. The completed-square kernel and Tonelli arguments need no mathematical change.

F2 and step 3.1 now attribute AC to the exact Brownian variation corollary consumed in F1. The same outcome omega still simultaneously yields uniform dyadic quadratic variation and infinite total variation, so the deterministic continuous-path counterexample is unchanged and fully supported.

The title now names the iid stopped exit segments actually established in steps 4.1-6.1. The body already distinguishes those segments from the dependent nested remainders W^n, and its measurable path encoding, strong-Markov factorization, and fair-sign conclusion remain unchanged.

The counterexample now normalizes Brownian paths, proves ambient and G_L measurability of L from the eventually constant stopped path and the no-flat-interval property, and derives the contradiction through fixed Borel no-zero events. Its direct Gaussian-density use now also declares the transition-semigroup lemma dependency; the non-stopping-time proof remains valid.
